title: Command Injection via Unsanitized workflow_dispatch Input in update-remix-run-dev.js CI Workflow
comments: Fechado pela HackerOne como duplicate de #3545083 (report original submetido ~7 meses antes, ja avaliado e fechado como informative -- nao corrigido, nao pago). Mesmo asset (vercel/vercel, mesmos 2 arquivos), mesmo input (new-version via workflow_dispatch), mesma raiz (input sem sanitizacao chegando em execSync()). Analista notou framing diferente: nosso relatorio descreveu como OS command injection via metacaractere de shell; o original descrevia como expression injection -- mas julgou ser a MESMA instancia de vulnerabilidade nao corrigida, nao uma classe diferente.

title: Timing Side-Channel in Bootstrap Token JWS Verification via Non-Constant-Time HMAC Comparison (`cluster-bootstrap`'s `DetachedTokenIsValid`)
comments: Closed as duplicate of report #3612349 (an earlier report describing the identical DetachedTokenIsValid == vs constant-time issue, same line, same fix). #3612349 itself was previously closed Informative: timing measurements acknowledged at the local level, but no significant security impact concluded due to lack of demonstrated remote exploitation / no statistical significance over real network conditions. Triager explicitly noted our report is more extensive in its statistical analysis but acknowledges the same fundamental limitations we stated ourselves (no network-observable channel, no repeatable interaction within a single join attempt, no HMAC recovery/forgery demonstrated).

title: Incorrect Argument Order Breaks the Documented GraphQL `@requires` Authorization Flow (`@kiwicom/iam`)
comments: Fechado como duplicado de #3439366. Texto do triager: mesma causa raiz (ordem de argumentos incorreta na chamada isUserAuthorized dentro de visitFieldDefinition, token IAM parando na URL, URL IAM parando no header Authorization, TypeError). Sem bounty, sem disclosure.
